survivors.title: Alternative Provision (AP) due-diligence & ongoing-monitoring compliance for schools and MATs
survivors.problem: When a school places a pupil with an external alternative provider, KCSIE 2025 and 'Arranging Alternative Provision' (2025) require the placing school to (a) run pre-placement due diligence proving the provider's safeguarding checks, DBS, policies, insurance and risk assessments are in order, and (b) review each placement AT LEAST half-termly with minuted checks — while RETAINING full safeguarding liability. Schools do this in ad-hoc Word packs and spreadsheets, re-collecting the same evidence each term, with no central register, no expiry alerts (DBS/insurance lapse silently) and no audit trail for Ofsted. One gap can trigger a 'safeguarding not effective' inadequate judgement.
survivors.who_suffers: Designated Safeguarding Leads, inclusion/AP leads and MAT central compliance teams. ~24,000 schools, ~1,200 MATs. DfE estimates ~29,244 children in unregistered AP in 2025 (doubled since 2019). AP funded at ~£10k/place. Buyer = school or trust (DSL/business manager can purchase).
survivors.merged_evidence: DfE 'Arranging Alternative Provision' (2025) mandates half-termly reviews and full retained safeguarding duty. 29,244 children in unregistered AP in 2025, doubled since 2019, commissioners retain safeguarding duties under KCSIE 2025/Working Together 2023 (peopleseducationsolutions.co.uk; vwv.co.uk). Schools told to build a manual 'due diligence pack' and keep minuted half-termly reviews. A product search for dedicated school-AP due-diligence software returned ONLY generic corporate/AML tools and zero dedicated product.
survivors.why_promising: Falls between stools: MIS tracks pupils not providers; SCR tools cover internal staff; safeguarding tools (CPOMS, MyConcern) log incidents not provider due diligence. Recent and rapidly-tightening duty (KCSIE 2025/26 post-unregistered-AP scandals) so no incumbent has built for it. Buyer carries personal/legal liability, workaround is a spreadsheet, school-level budget avoids slow LA procurement, and a two-sided provider-profile network effect is available.
survivors.ai_unlock: AI ingests a provider's uploaded safeguarding policy/insurance/DBS evidence, auto-extracts dates/named DSL/gaps, flags missing or expiring documents, auto-generates the KCSIE-compliant due-diligence pack and the minuted half-termly review report, and lets providers self-serve a reusable verified profile many schools can pull from.
survivors.monetization: SaaS per school (~£300-800/yr) and per-MAT central licences (£2k-10k/yr for cross-trust oversight). Expansion: charge AP providers for a verified reusable assurance profile broadcast to commissioning schools (two-sided).

existing_solutions.note: LA-run quality-assured AP provider directories with annual QA audits. Manual/PDF, per-LA, not a school-purchasable SaaS, and don't cover the school's own retained-liability evidence trail.

survivors.defensibility: Weak-to-moderate. The compliance workflow itself is commoditisable (any incumbent — The Key, Every, Civica, LearnTrek — can bolt on a provider register + expiry alerts in a quarter). The only durable moat is a shared, network-effect provider directory: if one AP provider uploads its DBS/insurance/policy pack ONCE and every commissioning school pulls verified evidence from it, providers stop re-sending packs and schools get instant due diligence. That two-sided data asset (a national, continuously-verified AP provider register) is hard to replicate and gets stickier with scale. Without that, it's a feature, not a company.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Medium. Buildable solo in weeks (forms, document store, expiry-alert cron, audit log, PDF export — exactly the founder's strength). But UK schools are slow, budget-constrained, term-time-gated buyers with no urgency until an Ofsted visit looms; sales cycles are 1-3 terms. £1m ARR needs ~600-1,000 schools at ~£1-1.5k or ~150-250 MATs at central pricing — realistically 18-36 months of grinding bottom-up SEN/DSL sales with zero network. First paying pilot plausible within 3-6 months via cold outreach to DSLs/AP leads.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE — genuine, regulation-driven, under-productised UK gap (no dedicated AP-provider due-diligence+expiry-alert+audit-trail SaaS found), but it's a thin feature with low switching cost that incumbents can copy, and schools are slow low-ACV buyers; only PURSUE if built as a shared provider-register network, not a per-school form filler.

survivors.title: Grid connection queue & milestone compliance tracker for renewables/BESS developers
survivors.problem: Under the 2025-26 GB connections reform (Gate 2, Queue Management Milestones, Progression Commitment Fees), a developer's grid connection offer is TERMINATED if they miss evidence-based milestones (planning consent, land rights, financial commitment) by the contractual date — losing their place in a multi-year queue plus a forfeited security fee. Each project has hundreds of interdependent tasks across NESO, the DNO, ICPs and internal teams; developers and advisors run this on bespoke Excel 'Queue Management Tool' spreadsheets that fail as portfolios scale.
survivors.who_suffers: UK renewable/BESS developers and IPPs with pipeline portfolios (each holding one or more connection offers) plus the connections-advisory consultancies managing offers on their behalf. 700+ GW sits in the GB connection queue, so the population of tracked agreements is very large.
survivors.merged_evidence: Roadnight Taylor (a connections consultancy) describes managing ICPs requiring 'constant management and tracking' across 'hundreds of tasks' using a 'Queue Management Tool' spreadsheet (roadnighttaylor.co.uk). Ofgem/DESNZ Connections Action Plan and Ofgem reform package confirm new Queue Management Milestones with termination for non-progression and a Progression Commitment Fee/security; Ofgem's Dec 2025 Connections End-to-End Review confirms the regime is live and evolving.
survivors.why_promising: The milestone/penalty regime only became biting in 2025-26 so incumbents' tools predate it. NESO's portal is a submission system, not a developer-side compliance/deadline cockpit. Consultancies bill hours on manual tracking (no incentive to productise); generic PM software doesn't encode Gate 2 / milestone / PCF rules; the rules change often (deters big vendors, suits a fast solo builder). One lost connection (six/seven figures) dwarfs the subscription. Strong fit with the founder's infrastructure/energy interest.
survivors.ai_unlock: AI parses heterogeneous connection-offer letters and DNO/NESO milestone schedules (non-standard PDFs) into structured deadlines, auto-flags at-risk milestones, drafts the evidence packs DNOs require to prove progression, and keeps the rule-set current as Ofgem reforms land.
survivors.monetization: SaaS per active connection agreement tracked (£50-150/offer/month) or per-portfolio seat to developers; higher-tier white-label to connections consultancies. Recurring and deadline-driven.

existing_solutions.note: Confirms the status quo: a FREE downloadable Excel milestone calculator used inside a consultancy. Not a SaaS. This is the incumbent 'tool' being replaced, and validates the spreadsheet pain.

existing_solutions.name: Cora Systems / Quorum On Demand / Cleanview / UL
existing_solutions.note: Generic renewable dev-stage PM (permitting, land, interconnection milestones). None encode GB Gate 2 / QM termination regime natively.

existing_solutions.note: BESS market/revenue intelligence + pipeline databases. Track grid-connection status as a data field, but do not manage a developer's own per-project contractual milestone obligations/evidence/alerts. Could plausibly add a compliance module — watch-list threat.

survivors.defensibility: Moat is regulatory-domain depth + workflow lock-in, not technology. The durable asset is a continuously-maintained encoding of the GB connections regime (Gate 2 criteria, the 8 User Progression Milestones / Appendix Q dates, QM termination triggers, Progression Commitment Fee, exception process, DNO/ICP variants) plus the per-project task graph and evidence templates that map to NESO's Connections Portal — kept current as the rules churn (Ofgem's End-to-End Review is explicitly 'live and evolving'). That regulatory-tracking burden is exactly what deters generic PM tools and what a solo founder CAN out-execute by being narrow and fast. Becomes a system-of-record once a portfolio's milestone data lives in it (switching cost). NOT defensible on code/AI alone — fully commoditisable there. Weakness: a consultancy (Roadnight Taylor, TNEI, Decerna) or a data incumbent (Modo) could bolt this on, and Sitetracker could productise a GB module. So defensibility is real but time-boxed: win the niche before they bother.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow-to-medium. The regime is live NOW (Gate 2 offers issued late 2025; milestone dates biting through 2026-2030), so urgency exists and budgets are real (a missed milestone = lost queue place worth £millions + forfeited security fee). But this is B2B sold into a clubby, relationship-driven UK developer/IPP/consultancy market with no public pricing and procurement friction — the founder's lack of network/credentials is the binding constraint. Realistic path: 6-12 months to first paying design-partner (likely a small/mid developer or one consultancy reselling it), revenue plausibly £30-150k ARR year 1. £1m ARR needs ~30-80 portfolio customers or a handful of consultancy/IPP enterprise deals — achievable in principle given 700+GW in the queue, but gated by trust and distribution, not product.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE — genuinely under-served developer-side niche with live regulatory pain and real money at stake, but a solo 19-yr-old with no energy network faces a trust/distribution wall and beatable-but-time-boxed defensibility; pursue only as a wedge via one consultancy design-partner, not as a cold B2B SaaS.

survivors.title: SEND tribunal appeal pack + working-document assembler for council SEND legal teams
survivors.problem: When a parent appeals an EHCP decision, the local authority must, within statutory deadlines, produce a 'working document' (the EHCP with every requested amendment marked using formal tracked-change keys across Sections A-K) and a paginated, indexed, de-duplicated tribunal bundle. Miss the bundle deadline and the LA can be barred from proceedings. Appeals have risen ~8x in a decade to ~25,000/year and councils lose ~98% — yet must still assemble a full compliant pack per case. It's pure manual document labour (copy-paste between PDFs, Word tracked-changes, re-pagination) by scarce caseworkers under a 30-working-day response clock plus a 10-working-day bundle clock.
survivors.who_suffers: SEND/EHC casework and legal teams in the ~150 English upper-tier/unitary LAs, each handling dozens-to-hundreds of live appeals. Buyer = Head of SEND / SEND Operations Manager / Principal Education Lawyer with delegated budgets.
survivors.merged_evidence: Appeals rose 3,147 (2014/15) to 25,002 (2024/25) (CPS 'Suffocated by Tribunals'; BERA). LAs win ~1.7% of full hearings (Special Needs Jungle; BASW). LAs allocated £99.2m (2022/23) to appeal defence, now estimated >£200m/yr. LA-prepared working document (tracked keys) and bundle obligations + bar-from-proceedings risk documented at West Sussex SENDIASS and IPSEA (bundles bloating to 600+ pages with duplicates). Tribunals Statistics Quarterly Jul-Sep 2025 confirms record caseload.
survivors.why_promising: Incumbent LA case-management systems (Liquidlogic, Mosaic) are systems-of-record that store the case but do NOT generate the marked-up working document or assemble/de-dupe/paginate the bundle. SEND-appeal software targets the PARENT side. Spend is huge (£200m+) and the bottleneck is exactly the document-reasoning LLMs now excel at. Risk: council sales cycles are long — mitigate via 2-3 reference authorities and per-bundle pricing.
survivors.ai_unlock: LLMs read the original EHCP + parent's requested amendments and produce a section-by-section working document with tracked keys; ingest mixed PDFs (EP/OT/CAMHS reports, school evidence) into an indexed, paginated, de-duplicated bundle with auto-index; flag third-party data for redaction; draft a first-cut response to appeal.
survivors.monetization: Per-authority licence ~£12k-£40k/yr by appeal volume, justified against £200m+ aggregate spend and current interim-staff day rates. Optional per-bundle pricing for smaller districts. Natural expansion to the EHCP annual-review backlog (auto-amendment drafting against the 12-month/4-week/12-week statutory clocks).

existing_solutions.note: GenAI EHCP drafting/amendment tool ALREADY in 40+ LAs (~27% of 150). Co-designed with SEND teams, section-by-section plan editing, explicitly markets 'reducing tribunals'. existing_solutions.note: Auto pagination/indexing/bookmarks/hyperlinks/dedup for court & tribunal bundles. Commoditises the entire bundle-assembly half of this idea. On the market for LA in-house legal teams.

existing_solutions.note: Crowded field of UK court/tribunal bundling tools, all on Practice-Direction-compliant pagination/indexing. The bundle half is a saturated commodity.

survivors.defensibility: Thin and eroding. The SEND-specific working-document generator (A-K tracked-change keys) is the one genuine white space — no product does it today. But (1) the document logic is exactly what GenAI commoditises, (2) the bundle half is already a saturated commodity (Bundledocs/CaseLines/Case Center, several on G-Cloud and in LA legal teams), and (3) the buyer is mid-adoption of funded GenAI EHCP incumbents (Agilisys at 40+ LAs, GovMetric, VITA) for whom 'also produce the appeal working document' is an obvious roadmap bolt-on with an owned customer relationship, the plan data, and framework procurement standing. The only candidate moat would be a SEND-tribunal-specific corpus + deep workflow lock-in (drafting + working-doc + bundle in one compliant pipeline), but a solo founder with no LA references cannot build that faster than incumbents already inside the door, and special-category data + public-sector procurement (DPIA, ICO/LGA AI guidance, security) raise the entry bar sharply.
survivors.speed_to_revenue: Slow. Buyer = Head of SEND / Principal Education Lawyer in ~150 LAs — long public-sector cycles, DPIAs on special-category children's data, ICO/LGA AI procurement scrutiny, framework/G-Cloud listing, and security reviews. With zero references, network, or credentials (the founder's hard constraints), first paid pilot realistically 9-15 months out; competitive against funded GovTech already embedded. £1m ARR needs ~25-50 LAs at £20-40k each — reachable arithmetically but requires winning competitive procurements cold.
survivors.recommendation: MAYBE-leaning-KILL — Real, verified, painful LA-buyer problem (LA prepares working doc + bundle, genuine bar-from-proceedings risk, 25k appeals/yr), and the A-K working-document generator is true white space; but it is lightly-served-and-closing, not open: bundle half is a commodity, and funded GenAI EHCP incumbents (Agilisys 40+ LAs, GovMetric, VITA) own the exact buyer and can bolt this on. Poor go-to-market fit for a solo founder with no network against slow, reference-driven public-sector procurement. Pursue only as a narrow wedge sold INTO/alongside an incumbent or a shared LA legal service, not as a standalone cold-sale play.
